title: GitHub - Scronkfinkle/byob: Bring Your Own Brain - Local Agent Harness
excerpt: Bring Your Own Brain - Local Agent Harness. Contribute to Scronkfinkle/byob development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
Note

Heads up: this project, README included, is influenced heavily by AI agents. If LLM-flavoured prose isn't your thing, fair warning. Human-written docs will come once things settle.

A native desktop AI coworker for the model you already run. Point byob at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or a hosted API) and it works in a folder with you: reads and writes files, runs code, and builds spreadsheets, charts, documents and small apps beside the chat.

byob is desktop software, not a web page in a window: one program for Linux, macOS and Windows that draws its own interface on the GPU, with no Electron.

Recorded live against a local model (llama.cpp); the waits for the model are cut.

What it does

  • A real desktop app. One folder, about a 60 MB download with everything in it (13 MB for the slim build), and native file dialogs, drag and drop and keyboard shortcuts. The browser UI is the reverse of the usual arrangement: the same native interface compiled to WebAssembly, so a tab or your phone gets the identical app, live on the same session.
  • Your model, your machine. No bundled inference and no account: any OpenAI-compatible URL, or Claude over Anthropic's Messages API. First run finds local servers on their usual ports; tool calling falls back to prompt-based calls when the server has none.
  • Artifacts beside the chat. Spreadsheets (xlsx/csv), charts, Markdown documents, images and HTML apps, each with its version history.
  • Hands, with a leash. File tools, run_command and run_python (sandboxed on Linux); approval cards with diffs; undo per turn.
  • Reads, searches and remembers. PDF, Word and PowerPoint files; images, for models that can see; web search and page reading (Exa by default, or your own SearXNG, Brave or Tavily); notes kept across chats in plain Markdown; a step plan for long tasks.
  • Workspaces. A folder with its own settings and where commands run: this machine, a Nix dev shell or a Docker/Podman container. Settings layer global → workspace → chat.
  • Everywhere you are. byob --serve opens that session to browsers too; with tailscale serve it's on your phone.
  • Everything is a plugin. The prompt, the core tools, artifacts, spreadsheets, subagents and compaction are bundled plugins on the same API anyone gets. Plugins add tools, draw UI (panes, header chips, settings, cards), hook every stage of a turn, and run long-lived backends. byob can write and fix its own plugins from a chat.


The browser UI at phone width.

Install

cargo install byob                          # with the browser UI built in
cargo install byob --no-default-features    # slim: desktop only, a few MB smaller
nix build github:Scronkfinkle/byob          # or .#byob-slim

Release archives for Linux, macOS and Windows are on the releases page: byob-… has everything (the browser UI and byob-artifact-host, which draws HTML apps inline; keep it next to byob), and byob-slim-… is byob alone. cargo install doesn't build the renderer; without it, HTML apps open in your browser with one click. On Linux byob needs no GUI toolkit (file dialogs go through the XDG desktop portal or zenity; without either, drop files onto the window), and the renderer draws with the system's OpenGL (Mesa).

On macOS the builds aren't signed by an Apple developer yet. Fetched from a terminal, a release archive never meets Gatekeeper (use x86_64 instead of aarch64 on an Intel Mac):

v=0.3.6; curl -L https://github.com/Scronkfinkle/byob/releases/download/v$v/byob-$v-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | tar xz
./byob-$v-aarch64-apple-darwin/byob

Or take byob-…-apple-darwin.dmg and drag byob.app into Applications. Downloaded with a browser, macOS refuses to open it at first: try once, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (on macOS 14 and older, right-click → Open), or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/byob.app. Opened from Finder, byob starts in your home folder and finds your shell's tools (Homebrew, Nix).

Use

byob                                        # desktop window
byob --serve                                # + browser UI on http://127.0.0.1:7470
byob --headless                             # browser UI only, no window
byob --inference-url http://host:8080/v1 --model local
BYOB_API_KEY=sk-... byob                    # for hosted endpoints
BYOB_API_KEY=sk-ant-... byob --inference-url https://api.anthropic.com/v1 --model claude-opus-5-5
byob --workspace ~/projects/taxes           # start in the workspace for that folder

tailscale serve 7470                        # reach it from any device on your tailnet
byob --headless --allow-user you@example.com # only admit that Tailscale login

On first run byob shows Connect a model: servers it found on this computer's usual ports (llama-server 8080, Ollama 11434, LM Studio 1234, vLLM 8000), presets for those and for hosted APIs, and a Test connection button. What you connect becomes your default model. Settings → Models keeps every model you use: add several from one server at once (byob lists what the server has), give each a description, test, duplicate, pick the default, choose a vision helper, and a model for titles and summaries (a small, fast one will do). Subagents run on the chat's model unless you pick another: a Subagent model in Settings → Models (or per workspace or chat), an agent file's model: (a saved model's name works), or, for models you mark Offered to subagents, the main model itself, choosing by their descriptions. A model's Advanced settings set its context window, temperature, top_p, max tokens, effort (Claude) and extra JSON for every request, e.g. {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}. The model chip in the header switches the chat in view to another model.

Claude is spoken to over Anthropic's own Messages API, not its OpenAI compatibility layer: pick the Anthropic preset (or any URL on api.anthropic.com), and byob uses prompt caching, shows Claude's thinking, and keeps it across a tool loop. For an Anthropic-style endpoint elsewhere (a gateway), set "api": "anthropic" under inference in settings.json.

Chats are grouped by workspace: a folder byob works in, with its own settings. New chat (Ctrl/Cmd+N; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O in the browser) starts one in the workspace you're in; its arrow, or the + next to Workspaces, makes a workspace: open a folder you have (or drop one on the window) or start an empty one; where commands run waits under Advanced. Each chat keeps its unsent draft. Search (Ctrl/Cmd+F) filters the list by chat title and workspace name. Hover a workspace for + (a new chat there) and ⋯ (or right-click it); that menu and the sliders next to a chat's title show what's inherited and what's set there: model (one of your saved models), approvals, tool calling, compaction, subagents and their model, extra instructions.

Settings (Ctrl/Cmd+, or the bottom of the chat list) is a screen of its own: the chat list gives way to Back, a search field (any setting by name, what it does, or a word you'd use for it; Ctrl/Cmd+F) and the categories: Models (saved models and their roles), Chats (what every chat starts with: instructions, approvals, limits, context), Plugins and, on this device only, Appearance (light or dark, themes, accent, messages, theme files), Text & layout (zoom, sizes, fonts, density, accessibility) and Colours. Back or Esc returns to the chat as you left it.

Plugins

Settings → Plugins lists what the chat in view can use. Any bundled plugin can be forked to your own plugins and edited (Fork to edit), or just ask byob to change or write one: it has authoring tools, and a broken plugin's errors come back to the model so it can fix it.

  • docs/views.md: view trees, the UI plugins draw (panes, chips, cards, grids).
  • docs/plugins-backend.md: long-lived backends (Python or Rust) and hooks.
  • docs/environments.md: where commands run, and adding your own.
  • demos/: hands-on tours, each in a throwaway profile (demos/run.sh todo).
  • examples/plugins/todo-demo: a small plugin with a backend, a pane and cards to copy from.

Develop

nix develop          # or: direnv allow
cargo run -p byob    # launch the app
cargo xtask web      # build the browser UI; the next `cargo build` embeds it
cargo xtask ci       # full gate: fmt, clippy, tests, layers, no-tokio, wasm
nix build            # release package (byob + bundled web UI + the artifact host)

# HTML artifacts inline on the desktop: the Servo helper is its own workspace (AGENTS.md §3)
(cd host/artifact-host && cargo build --release)   # scripts/headless.sh picks it up

# desktop GUI on a virtual display, scripted, with a screenshot (HEADLESS_RECORD=x.mp4 records it)
scripts/headless.sh --inference-url http://localhost:8080/v1 --model local --send "hi" --screenshot /tmp/byob.png
scripts/readme-media.sh                            # regenerate this README's pictures

# live test against a real server
BYOB_LIVE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1 cargo test -p byob-llm -- --ignored

See AGENTS.md for the rules, docs/architecture.md for the design and ROADMAP.md for what's next. byob began as a rewrite of hob, an earlier desktop coworker that bundled llama.cpp; byob drops the bundled inference.

content_html_zh:
Note

Heads up: this project, README included, is influenced heavily by AI agents. If LLM-flavoured prose isn't your thing, fair warning. Human-written docs will come once things settle.

A native desktop AI coworker for the model you already run. Point byob at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or a hosted API) and it works in a folder with you: reads and writes files, runs code, and builds spreadsheets, charts, documents and small apps beside the chat.

byob is desktop software, not a web page in a window: one program for Linux, macOS and Windows that draws its own interface on the GPU, with no Electron.

Recorded live against a local model (llama.cpp); the waits for the model are cut.

它的作用

  • A real desktop app. One folder, about a 60 MB download with everything in it (13 MB for the slim build), and native file dialogs, drag and drop and keyboard shortcuts. The browser UI is the reverse of the usual arrangement: the same native interface compiled to WebAssembly, so a tab or your phone gets the identical app, live on the same session.
  • Your model, your machine. No bundled inference and no account: any OpenAI-compatible URL, or Claude over Anthropic's Messages API. First run finds local servers on their usual ports; tool calling falls back to prompt-based calls when the server has none.
  • Artifacts beside the chat. Spreadsheets (xlsx/csv), charts, Markdown documents, images and HTML apps, each with its version history.
  • Hands, with a leash. File tools, run_command and run_python (sandboxed on Linux); approval cards with diffs; undo per turn.
  • Reads, searches and remembers. PDF, Word and PowerPoint files; images, for models that can see; web search and page reading (Exa by default, or your own SearXNG, Brave or Tavily); notes kept across chats in plain Markdown; a step plan for long tasks.
  • Workspaces. A folder with its own settings and where commands run: this machine, a Nix dev shell or a Docker/Podman container. Settings layer global → workspace → chat.
  • Everywhere you are. byob --serve opens that session to browsers too; with tailscale serve it's on your phone.
  • 一切都是插件。 The prompt, the core tools, artifacts, spreadsheets, subagents and compaction are bundled plugins on the same API anyone gets. Plugins add tools, draw UI (panes, header chips, settings, cards), hook every stage of a turn, and run long-lived backends. byob can write and fix its own plugins from a chat.

The browser UI at phone width.

安装

cargo install byob                          # with the browser UI built in
cargo install byob --no-default-features    # slim: desktop only, a few MB smaller
nix build github:Scronkfinkle/byob          # or .#byob-slim

Release archives for Linux, macOS and Windows are on the releases page: byob-… has everything (the browser UI and byob-artifact-host, which draws HTML apps inline; keep it next to byob), and byob-slim-… is byob alone. cargo install doesn't build the renderer; without it, HTML apps open in your browser with one click. On Linux byob needs no GUI toolkit (file dialogs go through the XDG desktop portal or zenity; without either, drop files onto the window), and the renderer draws with the system's OpenGL (Mesa).

On macOS the builds aren't signed by an Apple developer yet. Fetched from a terminal, a release archive never meets Gatekeeper (use x86_64 instead of aarch64 on an Intel Mac):

v=0.3.6; curl -L https://github.com/Scronkfinkle/byob/releases/download/v$v/byob-$v-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | tar xz
./byob-$v-aarch64-apple-darwin/byob

Or take byob-…-apple-darwin.dmg and drag byob.app into Applications. Downloaded with a browser, macOS refuses to open it at first: try once, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (on macOS 14 and older, right-click → Open), or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/byob.app. Opened from Finder, byob starts in your home folder and finds your shell's tools (Homebrew, Nix).

Use

byob                                        # desktop window
byob --serve                                # + browser UI on http://127.0.0.1:7470
byob --headless                             # browser UI only, no window
byob --inference-url http://host:8080/v1 --model local
BYOB_API_KEY=sk-... byob                    # for hosted endpoints
BYOB_API_KEY=sk-ant-... byob --inference-url https://api.anthropic.com/v1 --model claude-opus-5-5
byob --workspace ~/projects/taxes           # start in the workspace for that folder

tailscale serve 7470                        # reach it from any device on your tailnet
byob --headless --allow-user you@example.com # only admit that Tailscale login

On first run byob shows Connect a model: servers it found on this computer's usual ports (llama-server 8080, Ollama 11434, LM Studio 1234, vLLM 8000), presets for those and for hosted APIs, and a Test connection button. What you connect becomes your default model. Settings → Models keeps every model you use: add several from one server at once (byob lists what the server has), give each a description, test, duplicate, pick the default, choose a vision helper, and a model for titles and summaries (a small, fast one will do). Subagents run on the chat's model unless you pick another: a Subagent model in Settings → Models (or per workspace or chat), an agent file's model: (a saved model's name works), or, for models you mark Offered to subagents, the main model itself, choosing by their descriptions. A model's Advanced settings set its context window, temperature, top_p, max tokens, effort (Claude) and extra JSON for every request, e.g. {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}. The model chip in the header switches the chat in view to another model.

Claude is spoken to over Anthropic's own Messages API, not its OpenAI compatibility layer: pick the Anthropic preset (or any URL on api.anthropic.com), and byob uses prompt caching, shows Claude's thinking, and keeps it across a tool loop. For an Anthropic-style endpoint elsewhere (a gateway), set "api": "anthropic" under inference in settings.json.

Chats are grouped by workspace: a folder byob works in, with its own settings. New chat (Ctrl/Cmd+N; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O in the browser) starts one in the workspace you're in; its arrow, or the + next to Workspaces, makes a workspace: open a folder you have (or drop one on the window) or start an empty one; where commands run waits under Advanced. Each chat keeps its unsent draft. Search (Ctrl/Cmd+F) filters the list by chat title and workspace name. Hover a workspace for + (a new chat there) and ⋯ (or right-click it); that menu and the sliders next to a chat's title show what's inherited and what's set there: model (one of your saved models), approvals, tool calling, compaction, subagents and their model, extra instructions.

Settings (Ctrl/Cmd+, or the bottom of the chat list) is a screen of its own: the chat list gives way to Back, a search field (any setting by name, what it does, or a word you'd use for it; Ctrl/Cmd+F) and the categories: Models (saved models and their roles), Chats (what every chat starts with: instructions, approvals, limits, context), Plugins and, on this device only, Appearance (light or dark, themes, accent, messages, theme files), Text & layout (zoom, sizes, fonts, density, accessibility) and Colours. Back or Esc returns to the chat as you left it.

插件

Settings → Plugins lists what the chat in view can use. Any bundled plugin can be forked to your own plugins and edited (Fork to edit), or just ask byob to change or write one: it has authoring tools, and a broken plugin's errors come back to the model so it can fix it.

  • docs/views.md: view trees, the UI plugins draw (panes, chips, cards, grids).
  • docs/plugins-backend.md: long-lived backends (Python or Rust) and hooks.
  • docs/environments.md: where commands run, and adding your own.
  • demos/: hands-on tours, each in a throwaway profile (demos/run.sh todo).
  • examples/plugins/todo-demo: a small plugin with a backend, a pane and cards to copy from.

发展

nix develop          # or: direnv allow
cargo run -p byob    # launch the app
cargo xtask web      # build the browser UI; the next `cargo build` embeds it
cargo xtask ci       # full gate: fmt, clippy, tests, layers, no-tokio, wasm
nix build            # release package (byob + bundled web UI + the artifact host)

# HTML artifacts inline on the desktop: the Servo helper is its own workspace (AGENTS.md §3)
(cd host/artifact-host && cargo build --release)   # scripts/headless.sh picks it up

# desktop GUI on a virtual display, scripted, with a screenshot (HEADLESS_RECORD=x.mp4 records it)
scripts/headless.sh --inference-url http://localhost:8080/v1 --model local --send "hi" --screenshot /tmp/byob.png
scripts/readme-media.sh                            # regenerate this README's pictures

# live test against a real server
BYOB_LIVE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1 cargo test -p byob-llm -- --ignored

See AGENTS.md for the rules, docs/architecture.md for the design and ROADMAP.md for what's next. byob began as a rewrite of hob, an earlier desktop coworker that bundled llama.cpp; byob drops the bundled inference.
